subject: general
question: The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, aims to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**limit global temperature rise**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Paris Agreement, adopted in December 2015, is a landmark international treaty under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) designed to combat climate change and its adverse effects globally.
 
• The primary goal of the Paris Agreement is to limit the global average temperature increase to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit the rise to 1.5°C.
 
• The agreement emphasizes the importance of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, with countries committing to implement Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and to enhance their climate action plans over time.
 
• It also focuses on strengthening resilience to climate impacts, promoting sustainable development, and providing financial support to developing nations for climate action.
 
• The Paris Agreement establishes a universal framework, recognizing the differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities of developed and developing countries in addressing climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Halt desertification:**

 
 
• Desertification refers to the degradation of land in arid, semi-arid, and dry sub-humid areas due to factors such as climatic variations and human activities.
 
• While combating desertification is an important environmental goal under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), it is not the primary focus of the Paris Agreement.
 
• Efforts to address desertification often involve sustainable land management practices, afforestation, and soil conservation techniques.
 
 
 
• **Eliminate air pollution:**
 
 
• Air pollution refers to the presence of harmful substances, such as particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, and sulfur dioxide, in the atmosphere.
 
• While reducing greenhouse gas emissions indirectly helps improve air quality, the Paris Agreement does not specifically aim to eliminate air pollution.
 
• Air pollution is primarily addressed through national policies, regulations, and programs like the World Health Organization’s air quality guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Promote water conservation:**
 
 
• Water conservation involves the sustainable management and use of water resources to ensure availability for future generations.
 
• Although water conservation is a critical environmental priority, it is not a direct objective of the Paris Agreement.
 
• Water conservation is often addressed through national and regional initiatives, such as watershed management, efficient irrigation practices, and rainwater harvesting.
